root_cause.text: The `get_upper_ifindexes()` function lacked bounds checking when writing upper device indices into a caller-supplied array, combined with an incorrect assumption that the number of upper devices would never exceed `MAX_NEST_DEV`, allowing unbounded iteration to write beyond the stack-allocated array bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `max` parameter to `get_upper_ifindexes()` and introduces an explicit bounds check (`if (n >= max) return -EOVERFLOW;`) before writing each index. The callers allocate `excluded_devices[1+MAX_NEST_DEV]` on the stack but the original function had no mechanism to enforce this limit. The patch passes `ARRAY_SIZE(excluded_devices) - 1` as the max parameter and checks for negative return values, demonstrating that the original code could write beyond the allocated buffer when more than 8 upper devices (e.g., many macvlans) existed.

Date:   Sat Jul 31 05:57:35 2021 +0000

    bpf, devmap: Exclude XDP broadcast to master device
    
    If the ingress device is bond slave, do not broadcast back through it or
    the bond master.
    
    Signed-off-by: Jussi Maki <joamaki@gmail.com>
    Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20210731055738.16820-5-joamaki@gmail.com

diff --git a/kernel/b
bic_trace_step.reason: The `get_upper_ifindexes()` function (lines 576-586) iterates through upper devices using `netdev_for_each_upper_dev_rcu()` and writes indices into the `indexes` array with `indexes[n++] = upper->ifindex;` without any bounds checking. The comment states 'indexes' must be able to hold at least MAX_NEST_DEV elements, but there is no validation that `n` stays within bounds. In `dev_map_enqueue_multi()` (line 591), the caller allocates `int excluded_devices[1+MAX_NEST_DEV];` (line 593), but if the actual number of upper devices exceeds MAX_NEST_DEV, the unbounded write in `get_upper_ifindexes()` will overflow the stack-allocated array. The function lacks the critical bounds check that should prevent `n` from exceeding MAX_NEST_DEV before writing to the array.
